name: Ferrante vaginal estrogen
question: Do vaginal estrogen ring or cream reduce six-month urinary tract infection recurrence versus placebo cream in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Postmenopausal women with recurrent UTI (at least two in six months or three in one year); after amendment, at least one episode had to be culture-proven and others could be documented by urinalysis.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 112–113; Results, p 113

verdictNote: After slow recruitment, ring and cream were pooled; nine withdrawals counted as endpoint failures.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with recurrent UTI, pooled vaginal estrogen ring or cream reduced six-month UTI or withdrawal versus placebo cream (11/18 versus 16/17; P = 0.041), with withdrawals counted as failures.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.dateLocator: Publisher article record, online-ahead-of-print note; print issue February 2021
reports.citation: Ferrante KL, Wasenda EJ, Jung CE, et al. "Vaginal Estrogen for the Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infection in Postmenopausal Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2021;27(2):112-117. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000749
reports.followUp: six-month randomized comparison, then optional six-month open-label estrogen

results.endpoint: Symptomatic culture-positive UTI or withdrawal by six months
results.measure: Intention-to-treat primary outcome; withdrawals counted as failures
results.note: The abstract reports 11/18; the Results paragraph prints 9/18 (50%), inconsistent with 8/15 completers with UTI plus three estrogen withdrawals. Revised two-sided significance level was 0.05; no effect estimate or confidence interval was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 112; Analysis, Amendments and Results, p 113

results.endpoint: Urinary tract infection by six months among completers
results.note: As-treated analysis of the 26 women who reached the primary outcome.

results.endpoint: Symptomatic UTI by six months: estradiol-ring subgroup
results.measure: As-treated completer subanalysis versus placebo cream
results.note: Formulation subanalysis; the study was not designed to compare the two active formulations.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 113; Discussion, p 114

results.endpoint: Symptomatic UTI by six months: conjugated-estrogen-cream subgroup
results.measure: As-treated completer subanalysis versus placebo cream
results.note: Formulation subanalysis; the study was not designed to compare the two active formulations.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 113; Discussion, p 114

harms.label: Treatment-related adverse events
harms.note: None reported among 34 women who initiated therapy; four unrelated events were described without arm assignments (two elective surgeries, one car accident, one acute myeloid leukemia diagnosis).
harms.locator: Full text, Results and Adverse Events, pp 113–114

delivery.label: Randomization and analysis
delivery.value: Initial 1:1:1 allocation to estrogen ring, estrogen cream, or placebo cream; after slow recruitment, the active arms were pooled and block randomization changed to 1:1, with a revised target of 48 women (35 randomized).
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Amendments, p 113

delivery.label: Withdrawal before six months
delivery.note: Percentages calculated from the pooled analysis denominators.

delivery.label: Formulations and dose
delivery.value: Estradiol ring containing 2 mg, placed vaginally every three months by study personnel; conjugated estrogen cream 0.625 mg/g, 0.5 g (0.312 mg) twice weekly at night; placebo lubricant cream 0.5 g twice weekly.

delivery.label: Six-month treatment adherence among completers
delivery.value: Ring present in 8/8 (100%); cream adherence in 4/7 (57.1%) by tube weight within 20% of expected.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 113; Results, p 114

relations.note: Both placebo-controlled trials found fewer recurrences with vaginal estrogen; Ferrante combined ring and cream arms.
Both found fewer recurrences with vaginal estrogen; Eriksen tested a ring against no estrogen treatment.
